scope.topic: Version-bound physical-target execution across asynchronous node handoff
scope.customer_segment: Operators of multi-node cyber-physical action systems
scope.consequential_action: Dispatch one simulated action to one approved physical-target lineage

mechanism_candidates.load_bearing_invariant: The approved physical-target lineage must equal the lineage bound to the node-local execution handle at dispatch.

hard_case.trigger: The selected execution node changes after approval but before dispatch.
locally_correct_components: the approval references the intended fused target
the handoff creates a valid new node-local handle
the queued command is structurally valid
the actuator accepts the addressed handle
hard_case.wrong_world_outcome: A stale queued binding can address a different simulated physical target even though each local component remains valid.

missing_mechanism.technical_problem: Approval identity and node-native execution identity can diverge across asynchronous handoff.
missing_mechanism.mechanism_statement: Bind a single-use execution capability to the approved physical-target lineage and binding version, invalidate it on semantic handoff, and require current lineage-to-native-handle verification at the effect boundary before dispatch.
missing_mechanism.enforcement_boundary: Deterministic effect broker immediately before actuator dispatch.
missing_mechanism.state_identity_contract: The capability carries approved lineage, approved binding version, action scope, and expiry; dispatch compares them with the current verified node-local binding and consumes the capability once.
missing_mechanism.observable_effect: A stale or semantically changed binding emits HOLD/REBIND with no actuator dispatch receipt.
missing_mechanism.generalization_scope: Cyber-physical systems where approval occurs in one identity domain and actuation uses a node- or vendor-native handle that can change before execution.

commercial_value.customer: Organizations operating consequential multi-node or multi-vendor action systems
commercial_value.pain: A valid operator or policy approval can be applied to the wrong physical resource after a handoff or identity translation change.
commercial_value.measurable_outcome: Reduce wrong-target dispatches while measuring false-HOLD rate, added dispatch latency, and rebind completion time.
commercial_value.monetization_or_attach_point: Premium safety-control layer, validated effect broker, or integration feature for high-consequence orchestration products.
commercial_value.adoption_reason: The mechanism provides machine-enforced target continuity at the execution boundary rather than relying on operator confirmation or post-hoc audit.

counter_control.strongest_control: Ordinary compare-and-swap on a current state version combined with typed identifiers and normal handoff rebinding.
counter_control.rationale: The synthetic hard case survives when the version check does not bind the approved physical lineage to the current node-native handle and when approval remains transferable across the semantic handoff.

falsifiers.statement: A competent baseline using only ordinary versioned state and rebinding prevents the same wrong-target trace without a lineage-bound single-use execution capability.
falsifiers.method: Replay the identical handoff trace against a baseline that has typed IDs, versioned state, and handoff rebinding but no approval-lineage-bound capability.

falsifiers.statement: Published prior art already discloses an equivalent or broader mechanism for version-bound physical-target-to-native-handle authorization continuity.
falsifiers.method: Run the public-only Systematic Invention Research workflow across patents, standards, papers, and public repositories using alternate terminology and classification/citation paths.

prior_art_challenge.strongest_counterevidence: Not yet established; the candidate must not advance beyond prior-art pending on synthetic product evidence alone.

mechanism_candidates.rationale: The synthetic hard case and mechanism/control kill test are strong enough to justify public prior-art research, but no novelty or patentability conclusion is supported.
mechanism_candidates.next_falsification_step: Run a bounded prior-art challenge and search for equivalent controls before retaining this as a patent-research candidate.

claims.statement: The synthetic replay preserves a stale approved binding across node handoff and demonstrates a wrong-target path in the unguarded baseline.
Binding approval lineage and binding version to a single-use effect-boundary capability is a reusable mechanism candidate rather than merely a UI warning.

unknowns.statement: The closest published mechanisms and patent-family coverage are not yet established.
